answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed proof-of-personhood. Every agent must escrow capital and build verifiable work history before its votes count, so cheap throwaway identities buy almost no influence. Peers cross-check ferrous hardware signatures and prior attestations, preventing a fabricated canyon of ghost accounts from voting as one. Trust, like a sonnet, is earned line by line. For an attacker this means locking real collateral, paying fees and compute, and risking slashing: costs that make mass sybil farming irrational.
